permission.claude.acceptEdits: File edits and ordinary file actions are approved automatically. Everything else follows the existing CLI rules and a one-time approval.
permission.claude.auto: Claude judges the risk of each action and asks less often. Explicit confirmation rules and protected actions may still need approval. Depending on the model, the provider or an administrator policy it may be unavailable or fall back to manual confirmation.
permission.claude.default: Claude's manual confirmation mode. Reads and previously allowed actions run, and actions that need extra permission ask for a one-time approval.
permission.claude.fullAccess: Ordinary permission checks are skipped. Files and commands outside the project can be reached. Explicit deny rules and the actions the CLI always confirms still apply.
permission.claude.plan: Reads and plans first. It asks for approval before changing sources and applies the CLI's plan mode policy to exploration commands.
permission.codex.acceptEdits: Runs in a sandbox that can write to the working folder. Extra approval requests are not allowed.
permission.codex.default: Runs in a read-only sandbox. Extra approval requests are not allowed.
permission.codex.onRequest: Runs in a working folder sandbox. Commands that need extra permission can be approved once or denied in the app. Allowing network access alone does not guarantee access to keychain credentials.
permission.other.acceptEdits: Uses the CLI's accept-file-edits mode. Other permissions follow the CLI settings.
permission.other.default: Follows the CLI's default permission policy. It can do what the existing CLI settings allow.
permission.other.fullAccess: Runs without approval prompts. It can change files outside the project and run commands.
permission.other.plan: Reads and plans before changing code. It uses the CLI's plan mode.

settings.cliUpdate.sectionDescriptionMac: Updates Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLIs installed on this Mac using their existing install methods. With automatic updates on, the app checks again in the background every 6 hours while it runs, and changes apply from the next request.
settings.cliUpdate.sectionDescriptionWin: Updates Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLIs installed on this PC using their existing install methods.
settings.components.sectionDescription: Shows status and install commands for agent CLIs and required plugins.
settings.display.browserDescription: Starts Chromium together with the app. Takes effect after a restart. If Chromium crashes, the whole app can quit.
settings.display.languageMenuNote: The menu bar switches to this language the next time the app opens.
settings.display.statusLineDescription: Runs the statusLine command in settings.json and shows the result below the input. Tools like oh-my-claudecode HUD work as-is.
settings.mobileRemote.allowDescription: Mac and phone each connect to the relay server independently. No port forwarding or VPN required; the relay only passes ciphertext. The on state persists across app restarts.
settings.mobileRemote.allowToggle: Allow phone to connect to this Mac
settings.mobileRemote.detail.networkOffl: No network connection. Reconnects as soon as the network is back.
settings.mobileRemote.detail.relayUnresp: The relay stopped answering, so the connection is being reopened.
settings.mobileRemote.guide.step1: Start a relay server — deploy relay/ or follow the Oracle Cloud guide (docs/relay-oracle.md).
settings.mobileRemote.guide.step2: Enter the relay address above, click Apply, and turn on Mobile Remote.
settings.mobileRemote.guide.step3: Open Mighty Claude on your iPhone and tap Add Mac.
settings.mobileRemote.guide.step4: Scan the QR code or paste the pairing link.
settings.mobileRemote.legacyAppsDescript: When off, only apps with a device token can connect. Only phones with tokens can be revoked individually, so it is recommended to turn this off after all phones have been updated to the latest app. Phones connected only via key are disconnected immediately.
settings.mobileRemote.regenerateKeyHelp: Changes the QR code. Phones with device tokens stay connected; only legacy apps without tokens need to re-pair.
settings.mobileRemote.relayHint: Enter the relay server address. You can host one yourself using the relay/ folder in the repository (docs/relay.md).
settings.mobileRemote.revokeBodyKeyReset: The pairing key will also be regenerated, changing the QR code. To use this device again, re-pair with the new QR. Other devices with tokens remain connected.
settings.mobileRemote.revokeBodyLegacyAl: All phones paired as {name} must re-pair with the new QR.
settings.mobileRemote.revokeBodyLegacyTe: All phones paired as {name} will be disconnected.
settings.mobileRemote.revokeBodyTokenTem: {name}'s device token will be invalidated and disconnected immediately.
settings.mobileRemote.scanInstruction: Scan the QR code in your phone app, or paste a pairing link.
settings.modelDefaults.error.duplicate: This name is already registered for the same provider.
settings.modelDefaults.error.effortWitho: At least one effort level must be selected when effort support is enabled.
settings.modelDefaults.error.empty: Model name must not be empty.
settings.modelDefaults.error.invalid: The model name contains invalid characters or exceeds the maximum length.
settings.modelDefaults.error.reserved: 'default' is a reserved name and cannot be used.
settings.modelDefaults.error.unknownLeve: The effort levels include an unknown level.
settings.phaseModels.description: Set machine-wide model knobs for each run phase. A knob left at Default is decided by the CLI.
settings.phaseModels.effortNote: Effort appears only where the CLI takes one per phase. The execution effort is used when a pane has no effort of its own, and never with a model that does not take that level.
settings.phaseModels.error.jsoncNotObjec: The root value of config.jsonc is not a JSON object.
settings.phaseModels.error.yamlNotUtf8: config.yaml contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8.
settings.phaseModels.fileError: The settings file could not be read, so nothing was written: {path}
settings.providers.loginNote: Change login accounts in CLI Accounts below.
settings.providers.windowsDescription: Uses local Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI as-is. Log in and install via each CLI.
settings.run.approvalInApp: Actions that need extra permission can be allowed once or denied from the run window. Block rules declared in the CLI stay in effect.
settings.run.approvalUnsupported: This runner does not support in-app approval. The CLI may deny actions that need extra approval.
settings.run.fastModeNote: Fast is separate from thinking effort. It is available on supported models and accounts and increases usage.
settings.run.limitsNote: Leave these empty to pass no limit. Turns are 1–1,000 and the cost is greater than 0 and at most 10,000 USD.
settings.run.maxBudgetError: Enter the cost limit as an amount greater than 0 and at most 10,000.
settings.run.maxTurnsError: Enter the maximum turns as a whole number between 1 and 1,000.
settings.run.modelSourceCli: CLI-provided model list · invocation access unverified
settings.run.modelSourceDefault: Default model list · availability depends on your account
settings.run.shellNetworkAcceptEdits: Network access for shell commands. Keychain credential access is a separate permission and may require additional approval in Ask for approval mode.
settings.run.shellNetworkFullAccess: With full access this switch does not restrict the network.
settings.run.shellNetworkLocked: Choose Working folder or Ask for approval permissions to set shell network access.
settings.run.title: Run settings
settings.run.unsupportedNotice: Extra settings this runner does not support are saved.
settings.run.webSearchDescriptionCached: The web search tool uses cached results.
settings.run.webSearchDescriptionDefault: Follows the web search setting stored in the CLI.
settings.run.webSearchDescriptionDisable: The web search tool is not used.
settings.run.webSearchDescriptionLive: The web search tool uses live results.
settings.screenShare.controlBody: {device} will be able to use this Mac's mouse and keyboard. When the phone first starts control it sends a key, and this Mac shows that key's fingerprint. Enrol it only if it matches the fingerprint on the phone's screen.
settings.screenShare.description: Only phones you allow can see or control this Mac's screen. This Mac makes every allow and access decision, and a newly paired phone starts switched off.
settings.screenShare.keyMissing: No control key is enrolled yet. When the phone first starts control, this Mac asks you to confirm its fingerprint.
settings.screenShare.legacyUnsupported: Older apps cannot be told apart from one another, so they do not support screen sharing. Update the phone app and pair again.
settings.screenShare.permissions.accessi: Needed to pass the phone's taps, scrolls and keys to this Mac. Viewing alone works without it.
settings.screenShare.permissions.intro: A phone needs these permissions to see and control this Mac's screen. Each button opens the System Settings pane that turns the permission on.
settings.screenShare.permissions.localNe: Needed to connect straight to a phone on the same Wi-Fi. Without it the video detours through the TURN server. When macOS does not reveal the state it shows as "Can't tell".
settings.screenShare.permissions.notific: Needed to show a notice on this Mac when a phone starts viewing or controlling it.
settings.screenShare.permissions.screenR: Needed to send the screen to the phone. After turning it on, you may have to reopen the app before it takes effect.
settings.screenShare.permissions.signing: The first install after the app's signing changed asks for Screen Recording and Accessibility once more. Even if Mighty Claude is already on in the list, you may have to switch it off and on again.
settings.screenShare.permissions.title: Mac permissions for screen sharing
settings.screenShare.removeKeyBody: Any control session from {device} ends. The next time the phone takes control it registers its key again, and this Mac asks you to confirm its fingerprint again.
settings.screenShare.scene.description: Opens a window of its own on the main display: after 3 s it scrolls a document and types into a terminal for 60 s, then holds a still screen for 30 s. It touches no other app or document, and connected phones mark each phase in their measurement export.
settings.styles.description: Built-in styles are always available. User-registered files and files found in repositories are only used after their contents have been reviewed once.
settings.styles.lockBanner: Edit or delete this file directly, then rescan. Until then, allow and revoke actions are not saved.
